# Best open-ear earbuds for running

| Need | Pick | Price in the sources | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Best overall | Bose Ultra Open Earbuds | $199 (list $299) | Clear sound, comfortable, stays put, physical buttons |
| Best bone conduction | Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 | $180 list, $125 at some retailers | Most open ears, 12-hour battery |
| Best for long or wet runs | Shokz OpenDots 2 | $200 | 10-hour battery, IP57 |
| Best value | Nothing Ear (Open) | $99 at Amazon (MSRP $149) | Strong bass for the category, IP54 |
| Cheap way to try the style | JLab Flex Open | about $40 | Low risk, decent comfort |

## Details

- **Bose Ultra Open:** Runner's World named it best overall, and WIRED says it has a clearer, more defined sound than most competitors. The physical buttons are easier to use mid-run than touch controls. Drawbacks are 7 hours of battery, IPX4 water resistance, and a price that makes them hard to justify for the sound alone. Runner's World also says Bose plans new open-ear earbuds within a month, so you could wait for those or for discounts on this pair. ([Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/))
- **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2:** WIRED calls it the best choice if you want more bass and power but still want to hear your surroundings. It has physical controls, USB-C, and an IP55 rating. The neckband can clash with long hair, ponytails, and winter hats. Clarity is a step behind the Bose. ([WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/), [RTINGS comparison with Bose](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946))
- **Shokz OpenDots 2:** WIRED's top pick overall. It lasts 10 hours per charge (40 with the case), is rated IP57, and leaves the top of your ear free for glasses or a hat. It's pricey, and Runner's World says the volume could be better. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/))
- **Nothing Ear (Open):** SoundGuys' top open-ear pick and its choice for best workout earbuds for running. It has a parametric EQ and multipoint pairing. ([SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/))
- **Budget:** The JLab Flex Open has less bass and detail than pricier pairs and touch-only controls, but it's a cheap way to see if clip-ons suit you. Runner's World lists it at $40 but says $50 in its verdict text, so check the price. WIRED also likes the $50 Soundpeats PearlClip Pro. ([Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/))

## Another budget option: Soundcore AeroFit 2

It has an ear-hook design, a 10-hour battery, and IP55 protection, and SoundGuys names it the best budget pick. SoundGuys lists it at $79.99 at Amazon. A coupon page, Dealectric, lists a $129.99 store price and says code AFSC20 takes it to about $104 at Soundcore's store. Those figures don't match, so compare prices before using the code. That link is an affiliate link, which means Dealectric earns a commission. ([Buy at Soundcore](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2), [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/))

## Where to buy

I don't have direct retailer links for the other models in these search results. The review pages above list current Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, and Bose or Shokz links, and prices change often.

Open-ear designs don't guarantee safety, so keep the volume low enough to hear traffic.

My pick for most runners is the Bose Ultra Open. If you want bone conduction or the most awareness, get the OpenRun Pro 2. If you're on a budget, get the Nothing Ear (Open) or the AeroFit 2.
